title: Run the 30-day outcome and investment review for internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace
summary: Use 30 days of product, support, performance, research, and cost evidence to decide the next investment for `internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace`.
acceptance_criteria: Run a 30-day outcome and investment review for `internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace` after users or operators experience `open repository-backed design truth, place screens and diagram objects, select and transform them, connect flows, inspect source context, and save`.
State the decision being made and the credible alternatives, including no further investment.
Use current product, usage, support, research, performance, assurance, cost, and maintenance evidence.
Separate eligible, exposed, activated, first-value, meaningful-value, repeated-value, retained, opted-out, support-needed, and unavailable states.
Separate observed behavior, participant feedback, researcher interpretation, and product hypothesis.
Include sample-size, selection-bias, seasonality, novelty, version, and instrumentation limitations.
Include accessibility, localization, privacy, security, reliability, support, and performance guardrails.
Include Jan's time, local hardware use, model cost, infrastructure, platform fees, and ongoing maintenance.
Evaluate monetization posture `internal-now-optional-commercialization-later` without assuming revenue is required.
Evaluate whether lifecycle `build` should continue, change, pause, consolidate, grow, maintain, or retire.
For internal tools, evaluate real workflow adoption and avoided effort rather than vanity usage.
For personal products, treat private usefulness and maintenance burden as valid outcomes.
For consumer products, evaluate value and trust before conversion optimization.
For fusion candidates, compare standalone and embedded mental models, permissions, performance, and rollback.
Record unresolved risks and evidence gaps.
Preserve the original hypothesis and prior decisions.
Produce an immutable decision with owner, date, rationale, evidence, and reconsideration trigger.
Create follow-up tickets only for approved next steps.
Do not change lifecycle, pricing, release, integration, or repository state automatically.
Update roadmap and portfolio projections only after human approval.
Archive invalidated research or telemetry through supersession rather than deletion.
Finish decision tooling and artifacts with zero app-owned warnings.
